what_it_does: Scientific instruments and computer simulations produce massive 3D data — dense arrays of numbers representing properties at millions of points in space, or mesh files encoding physical geometry. Visualizing this data is challenging because it is too large to fit on a single computer, and traditional visualization tools lack collaborative and immersive capabilities. This paper presents ASCRIBE-XR, a Virtual Reality application that enables scientists to explore large scientific datasets immersively by wearing VR headsets. The system connects to high-performance computing (HPC) clusters running on supercomputers — the computation-heavy systems physically located in labs — allowing the VR interface to tap into remote supercomputing power for processing massive datasets while streaming results back for real-time 3D visualization. Multiple scientists can view and interact with the same 3D visualization simultaneously over the internet using WebRTC (real-time communication protocol) and MQTT (messaging protocol), enabling collaborative discovery sessions.
